t: You're outside the Noël Coward Theatre, in St Martin's Lane, a West End theatre now named for the playwright, composer and actor. It opened on 12 March 1903 as the New Theatre, built by Sir Charles Wyndham behind Wyndham's Theatre, which was finished in 1899. It was designed by W. G. R. Sprague, with a classical exterior and a Rococo interior. Sprague trained under Frank Matcham and designed at least thirty-five theatres, and eleven of his surviving London theatres are listed. It was later known as the Albery Theatre.
